Translations.KeyConceptsAndRules: Read scales with 2, 4, 5 or 10 equal intervals and explain how the interval value determines a pointer reading.
Translations.WorkedExamples: Example A: A scale from 30 to 80 has 5 equal intervals. Each interval is 10, so a pointer three intervals after 30 reads 60.
Translations.StepByStepSolutions: Calculate one interval, multiply by the pointer position, add the start value, then check the full interval count reaches the end.
Translations.CommonMistakes: Do not compare numbers by looking at a single digit or by counting digits after the decimal point.
